caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 31 and 32 of 1994.
lawyer:
Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, Senior Advocate instructed by Serajur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record —For Petitioners in both the Petitions. 
Not represented—Respondents in both the Petitions.
parties:
Bangladesh Bank ----- Petitioner
vs.
Mustafizur Rahman and another ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mostafa Kamal J : Accused-respondent No. 1 Mustafizur Rahman filed applications for bail in Motijheel PS Case Nos. 12(8)/92 and 45(11)/92 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who, by separate orders, dated 13-7-93, rejected the applications for bail. Respondent No. 1 then preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1264 of 1993 and Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1263 of 1993 respectively against the said orders of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. By separate judgments dated 21-7-93 the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka dismissed the Miscellaneous Cases on the ground that the respondent's earlier prayers for bail were rejected by the High Court Division once and therefore it is risky for the Sessions Court to release the respondent on bail. The respondent can move the High Court Division for bail if he has any new grounds. The respondent is not entitled to bail at this stage in the public interest. The economic interest of Bangladesh is involved in the charge of misappropriation against him. 

 2. The respondent then preferred Miscellaneous Case Nos. 1252 and 1253 of 1993 in the High Court Division against the said orders of the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka. By separate judgments dated 9-3-94 the same Division Bench of the High Court Division made the Rules absolute and released the respondent on bail in both the Motijheel PS cases on the grounds, inter alia that the learned Session Judge has not given any reason while rejecting bail which is mandatorily required to be given under the first proviso to the substituted section (5) of section 167 CrPC as amended by the Code of Criminal Procedure (Second Amendment) Act, 1992. Also, no reason has been assigned as to why the Investigating Agency failed to submit the charge-sheets within a period of one year and six months after the receipt of the FIR. The High Court Division found that the Bangladesh Bank suspended all the operations of the company, namely, BCI Ltd. in connection with which the alleged misappropriation took place and the Bangladesh Bank has taken possession of the papers and documents under its control. In such circumstances if the respondent is released on bail, it opined, he will not be in a position to tamper with the evidence. 

 3. The informant in both the PS cases, Bangladesh Bank, has preferred these two petitions for leave to appeal from the said judgments and orders of the High Court Division. 

 4. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Counsel for the informant-petitioner, submits that it is not factually try that the learned Sessions Judge has not given any reason in rejecting the respondent's two applications for bail in the two Motijheel PS cases concerned. The learned Sessions Judge has stated that the charges leveled against the respondent are connected with the economic interest of Bangladesh and at this stage he is not entitled to bail in the public interest. 

 6. When asked Dr. Rafiqur Rahman submits that he has no instructions if charge-sheets have been submitted against the respondent in the two Motijheel PS cases.
